si_4_title.answer: Beyond homogeneity: charting the landscape of heterogeneity in neurodevelopmental and psychiatric electroencephalography

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS) were used to model the relationship between EEG features and age. Fractional polynomials were employed as smoothing functions to account for non-linearity.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: For each feature, we split our reference population (HC) into training and test sets, and trained a Generalized Additive Model for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS) on the training set. ... Bethlehem et al. use fractional polynomials as the smoothing function to account for nonlinearity without adding instability to their models [24], and we adopt the same approach.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled two sets of features: EEG power spectra (PSD) calculated using Welch's method (relative power in delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma bands) and functional connectivity estimated using Amplitude Envelope Correlation (AEC) between 68 brain regions (Desikan-Killiany atlas).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: For the spectral features, a GAMLSS was fitted to the relative power (Welch ' s method) of each channel and each frequency band. Functional connectivity was estimated between 68 prede /uniFB01 ned brain regions from the DesikanKilliany atlas using Amplitude Envelope Correlation -AEC- [36, 37], corrected for source leakage using an orthogonalization approach [38].

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was the main covariate, modeled using fractional polynomials (implying non-integer terms). Sex and Site were included as covariates in specific models based on BIC selection (Sex for Alpha band connectivity; Site for Theta, Alpha, and Beta band spectral power).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In this study, our response variable is an EEG-derived feature and the main covariate is age. The possibility of adding other covariates such as sex and data collection sites is detailed in the following sections. ... Table S5 | Model equations... y ~ fp (age, 1) + factor (site) ...
